subject: How each tool reaches Claude Code on a flat-rate subscription
method: read of the installed Headroom source; no benchmark claim is made about their compression ratio

headroom.posttooluse_hook: ABSENT - zero occurrences of PostToolUse/updatedToolOutput in the package
headroom.reversible_recall: CCR (Compress-Cache-Retrieve) via headroom/ccr/tool_injection.py - injects a retrieval tool

distil.claude_code_path: proxy (wrap) AND, as of this branch, a first-party PostToolUse hook
distil.posttooluse_hook: PRESENT - proven live: tool_result 18,214 -> 11,178 bytes, answer unchanged
distil.reversible_recall: digest + distil_expand on METERED only; declined on subscription
distil.decision_equivalence_proof: certificate + gate (shadow, SIG v3, conformal bounds)

the_difference: Headroom achieves reversibility on subscription by injecting a retrieval tool through a proxy that intermediates OAuth-authenticated traffic. distil declines that posture on ToS grounds (Anthropic Consumer Terms section 3 item 7 restricts automated access on subscription credentials) and instead uses a documented first-party extension point, which cannot rewrite history and therefore cannot support recall - making lossless-only the correct AND the compliant tier.
not_claimed: No head-to-head compression-ratio benchmark was run against Headroom.
No claim that Headroom violates any terms - only that distil chose a different risk posture.
Headroom's quota telemetry is the better idea and distil adopted it.
